Question: past every way that the device keeps at once (more blocks than any of the four ways of FORCE_WAYS
holds), the force kernel of se_e2_a takes the narrow blocks without the sums across the warps (sums_past false
for se_e2_a, true for se_e2_r). In the ways run of #45 the HAP model's 968 centers took 553.2 us that way and
534.5 us with the sums (3.4% less), water's 1,536 atoms 0.6% more with them. Larger passes were not tried.
Settings, one build: def (as it chooses), sums (--block-sums 1000000: the sums in every pass; past every way that
is the narrow blocks with the sums, which is what sums_past true would give), def2 (def again, the control).
Cases: se_e2_a passes past every way only (checked from the capacity line and the way in the bench lines), HAP
(the ensemble model of iteration 0, f32 with and without tables, f64 with tables) on batches of 88, 169 and 224
atoms, and water at 1,536, 12,288 and 98,304 atoms (f32 with and without tables, f64 with tables).
Measure: the least evaluation of each over the rounds (as the ways runs), the median beside it;
spread = |def2/def - 1| of the case.
Rule:
1. sums_past becomes true for se_e2_a if, in every case, sums is not slower than def by more than max(spread, 1%)
and in at least one HAP case it is faster by more than max(spread, 1%) (the change helps somewhere and hurts
nowhere).
2. If sums is faster in some cases and slower beyond the bound in others, sums_past for se_e2_a becomes a limit of
blocks (the sums past every way up to N blocks, N between the cases on either side), but only if the cases
faster and those slower are separated by size alone, the same in both precisions measured; otherwise nothing
changes.
3. If sums is nowhere faster beyond the bound, nothing changes, and the 968-center case is recorded as noise or a
model's quirk.

Rule 2 applied again, over all cases: float32 and float64 with tables from sums-1.json (their kernels unchanged),
the float32 exact nets from sums-2.json (the kernel that ships). A case is faster if sums against def is below
-max(spread, 1%), slower if above +max(spread, 1%), spread = |def2/def - 1|. Size is r = blocks / without, where
without is what the device keeps at once of the narrow blocks without the sums for that case (its capacity line).
- If every faster case has a smaller r than every slower case (and so in each precision), the limit
SE_E2A_SUMS_PAST_WAVES is the smallest multiple of 0.25 that is at least the largest r of a faster case, if that
is below the smallest r of a slower case, else the largest r of a faster case itself (to two decimals, rounded
down). With sums-1.json alone this gives 1.25 (largest faster r 1,056 / 896 = 1.18, smallest slower 1,792 / 896
= 2.0), the limit of commit 7d1dee4.
- If not, nothing changes past every way for se_e2_a: the limit goes to 0, the narrow blocks without the sums at
any size past every way, as before PR C.
One limit for every kernel of se_e2_a (the rule asks for one), each kernel held to its own `without`.
If the limit changes, rule 2 of run/prc/rule-ab.txt takes the new window (the cases of prc_ab.py whose blocks lie
within it) before any timing of the A/B, and the docs and tests follow the new value.

Amended 2026-11-23 00:26, before the run (no measurement of sums-2 has run), after a review of this rule:
1. One limit per kernel instead of one for every kernel of se_e2_a. The kernels of the tables (the one that looks
them up and the one that reads their rows stored, whose code PR C keeps) take theirs from the cases with tables
of sums-1.json by rule 2, as decision-sums-past.txt did (1.25: largest faster r 1,056 / 896 = 1.18, smallest
slower 1,792 / 896 = 2.0, the faster case of float64 at 896 / 768 = 1.17 below it). The kernel of the exact nets
(se_e2_a_exact_backward, a kernel of its own since PR C) takes its own from sums-2.json, by rule 2 over its cases
alone, both precisions together. Why: with one limit, one case of the exact nets beyond the bound (faster far
past, or slower just past) would take the sums from the kernels of the tables, whose gain was measured on code
that PR C does not change.
2. sums-2.json takes the exact nets in float64 as well (the same kernel; 16 lanes in float64 before PR C too): HAP
88 x {9, 11, 13, 16, 20} (792 to 1,760 blocks; the device keeps 768 of the narrow ones at once without the sums,
capacity line 256 384 384 768) and water at 1,536 atoms (256 512 384 768).
3. "else the largest r of a faster case itself (to two decimals, rounded down)" would leave out the very case that
sets it: it is rounded up to two decimals instead, which admits that case (to more decimals if two would reach
the smallest r of a slower case).
4. A case not past every way (its blocks at most what the device keeps of the narrow blocks at once without the
sums) is left out of the decision.
5. Where this rule or rule 2 of run/prc/rule-ab.txt says the limit goes to 0 (rule-ab.txt says 1.0, which past every
way is the same): that kernel takes the narrow blocks without the sums past every way, as before PR C, and the
code drops the rule for it instead of keeping a limit of 0.
tools/fit/decide_sums2.py applies this text as amended.
